chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one who informed him, from one of the two (peace be upon them both)

regarding the witnesses: when they testify against a man and then retract from their testimonies, and the judgement has already been passed upon the man, they are held responsible for what they testified with and are fined
However, if the judgement has not yet been passed, their testimonies are dismissed and the witnesses are not fined anything.

key_terms.الشُّهُود: Witnesses (shuhood) — those who provide sworn testimony in legal proceedings
key_terms.رَجَعَ عَنِ الشَّهَادَة: To retract testimony — withdrawing a previously given legal statement
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony (shahada) — formal witness statement in court
key_terms.ضُمِّنُوا: They are held responsible/liable — made to bear financial compensation (daman)
key_terms.غُرِّمُوا: They are fined/penalized — subjected to financial penalty
key_terms.قُضِيَ: Judgment was passed — the judicial ruling was executed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Islamic law when witnesses retract their testimony after judgment has been passed?
ai.summary: This hadith from one of the two Imams (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq, peace be upon them) establishes a key principle of Islamic judicial procedure: the legal consequences for witnesses who retract their testimony differ based on whether judgement has already been executed. If retraction occurs after execution, the false witnesses bear full financial liability for the harm caused. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential concern for accountability and compensation (damān) in legal proceedings, protecting defendants from unjust verdicts resulting from false or coerced testimony.
